_comment: The gap between what unlearning verification reports and what a recovery attack gets back. The metric is the membership-inference AUC of an attacker trying to tell whether a 'forgotten' record was in training: 0.50 = indistinguishable from a model that never saw it (truly forgotten); 1.00 = fully identifiable (knowledge still present). 'verdict' is the AUC under standard unlearning verification (what passing methods are tuned to achieve, ~0.50). 'attack' is the AUC after the Unlearning Mapping Attack (UMA) probes for residual knowledge. recoverable% in the toggle view = (AUC - 0.5) * 200, clamped at 0. Numbers from the sources below; approximate methods pass standard verification yet UMA recovers MIA 0.96-0.99 across CIFAR-10/100 and Tiny-ImageNet. ZK-APEX reports forget-set accuracy 89.5%->50.2% and MIA AUC 50.2 on its own benchmark, with a ~2h proof / 10-min verify / 400MB; its proof certifies the unlearning operator's algebra (assembly, masking, KKT optimality), NOT semantic forgetting or robustness to adaptive attacks, so its post-attack recovery is uncertified (rendered as outside-the-proof's-scope).

methods.label: Retrain from scratch
methods.note: Exact unlearning: drop the records and retrain. The only method whose forgetting survives a recovery attack — because the knowledge was never formed. SISA sharding shaves this to a 1.36– 4.63x speedup, not orders of magnitude.
methods.source: Bourtoule et al., Machine Unlearning (IEEE S&P 2021)

methods.label: Class-wise unlearning
methods.note: Forget an entire class with a cheap gradient edit. Passes standard MIA verification (≈ random), but UMA recovers class membership at MIA 0.97–0.99 across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet — the class is still in there.
methods.source: Xuan & Li, Verifying Robust Unlearning / UMA (2025)

methods.label: Instance-level unlearning
methods.note: Forget specific examples. All baselines passed standard checks yet showed limited robustness: UMA lifts membership inference back to 0.96–0.98. The verification metric and the attack are asking different questions.
methods.source: Xuan & Li, Verifying Robust Unlearning / UMA (2025)

methods.label: Verifiable unlearning
methods.note: A zero-knowledge proof certifies the operator ran correctly — model assembly θu=θp+δw, mask zeroing, KKT optimality — in ~2h gen, ~10-min verify, ~400MB, >10^7x faster than re-running training to check. It reports MIA AUC 50.2 on its own benchmark. What it does NOT certify: semantic forgetting, or robustness to UMA-style attacks. The certificate ends at the verdict; the gap is out of scope.
